newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sets dates for 1997 APEC meetings.
newsitem.headline: Canada sets dates for 1997 APEC meetings.

text.p: Canada said on Wednesday that the 1997 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Vancouver would be held in the last two weeks of November.

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, set to leave for a trade mission to Asia, said the APEC leaders would hold their summit on Nov. 24 and 25, preceded by an APEC ministerial meeting on Nov. 22 and 23.
Canada this year chairs the 18-member APEC forum and plans a series of ministerial meetings to precede the November summit.

Meetings will be hosted on trade in Montreal on May 9 to 10, sustainable development in Toronto on June 9 to 11, transport in Victoria, British Columbia on June 22 to 24, energy in Edmonton, Alberta, on Aug. 27 to 29 and small and medium-sized enterprises in Ottawa on Sept. 18 to 19.
Canada will also hold preparatory meetings for APEC officials in Victoria, Quebec City and St. John's, Newfoundland, but the dates of these meetings were not released.

APEC comprises the United States, Canada, Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, the Philippines, Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Australia, Mexico, Papua New Guinea, New Zealand and Peru.
